--- title: "Deletion of the syllable /xa/" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_JA_TODAS_POSIC" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_JA_TODAS_POSIC`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Supresión de la sílaba «ja»*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_JA_TODAS_POSIC.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Deletion of the syllable /xa/, at age 6 (2,259 administrations in 3 cohorts). AUC .73 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1886 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 9 (1886) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child was instructed to delete a speech sound and to provide the remaining word or pseudoword. Correct responses, errors and time were recorded. | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_imagenes.png){width=45%} ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:----------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1886|Omitir sílabas |Un dibujo por pantalla | 9| 3|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 6| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1886.** 3 de entrenamiento + 9 de prueba. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/CF523.html) and [rapid naming](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/RAN.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.1| 2010| 152|2016/17 | 917| 263| 653| 34| | 6.1| 2011| 183|2017/18 | 781| 0| 781| 31| | 6.1| 2013| 898|2019/20 | 561| 402| 159| 35| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|----------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 6.1| 665| 2010, 2013| 8.69| 3.48| 10| -0.98| 3.31| 26.32| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–12 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 6.1| 665|0–12 |0–12 |0–12 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .93. ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .58. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (6.1, r = .50). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .73. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58–.62. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_JA_TODAS_POSIC_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .68 (1 time point; 679–679 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 6.1| 665| 2010, 2013| 2| 3| 4| 7| 10| 12| 12| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABA_JA_TODAS_POSIC_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 6.1| 2,246| 0.151| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.1| 2,252| 0.076| 0.073| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.1| 2,249| 0.049| 0.020| |School (ICC) | 6.1| 2,259| 0.182| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Deletion of the syllable /xa/” (code 1886; LEEDUCA battery) assesses syllable awareness (deletion in any position). Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 12 items. The time limit is 240 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .93 (N = 2,354, 12 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58–.62. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 6.1 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
